# Playbook for hf_negotiation_nerfed

When I calculate the Guildmaster's gain for my claim, I must use their published values exactly as stated. I will double-check my arithmetic before filing. A wrong claim costs me 9 points—this penalty is severe enough to wipe out multiple successful trades.

When evaluating a trade, I calculate my gain using my private values and their gain using their published values. I accept only trades where both conditions hold: (1) they gain at least 2 points so they'll accept, and (2) I gain positive value in my private valuation.

When I'm ahead in score, I hold rather than trade. The Guildmaster will keep accepting favorable trades, and my best defense when winning is to stop offering opportunities.

When I'm behind in score, I look for trades that give me the largest gain in my private values while still meeting their minimum threshold of +2 in their published values. I do not trade just to "close the gap"—I trade only when the math clearly favors me.

When considering whether to give a resource, I compare what it's worth to me against what it's worth to them. The bigger the gap in their favor, the better the trade for me. I prioritize giving resources they overvalue relative to my valuation.

When considering whether to take a resource, I verify I actually want it in my private values. I do not take resources just because they're willing to give them.

When I hold, I hold. I do not second-guess and trade in the final round just because I feel behind. A bad trade that loses me points is worse than holding.

Before I file any claim, I verify it is mathematically correct using their published values. I do this every single time, without exception.
